banner: 新模型规则：删规矩，信判断
banner_en: Anthropic's new rule for Claude 5: trust judgment, not rules

image.caption: 本期头条配图：Anthropic 官方博客用一幅手捧空白书的简笔画，给新规矩打了个比方。不是往书里塞满死板条文，而是信任读书的人（也就是模型本身）能看懂空白处该怎么填。文章里最实的一条数据是：给 Claude Code 用的系统提示词，官方直接砍掉了八成以上，跑分没有跌。（图：Anthropic 官方博客）
image.caption_en: This issue's lead image: Anthropic's blog illustrates its new rule with a simple sketch of a hand holding a blank book. Instead of stuffing the book with rigid rules, the idea is to trust the reader (the model itself) to know how to fill in the blank pages. The most concrete number in the piece: Anthropic cut Claude Code's system prompt for newer models by over 80%, with no drop in benchmark scores. (Image: Anthropic's official blog.)

actions.text: 今晚在自己常用的 Claude Code 项目里跑一次 `/doctor`，看看它对你的 CLAUDE.md 和 skills 会给出什么“精简”建议。Anthropic 今天这篇博客等于把自己的评分标准公开了：面向新一代模型，系统提示词里的老规矩，比如“注释不能超过一行”这种死规定，被换成“照抄周围代码的风格”这种更抽象的判断题，Claude Code 的系统提示词因此被砍掉八成以上，跑分反而没掉。具体做法：先跑`/doctor`，把它标出来的冗余、重复、可以交给模型自己判断的部分记下来；然后挑一条你自己写的、管得最细的规则，试着改成一句描述结果长什么样、而不是一步步该怎么做的话，跑一遍原来的任务看输出是不是还稳；如果输出变差了，说明这条细规则暂时不能删，先留着，但你验证过了，不是凭感觉。
actions.source: Hacker News · Anthropic：新一代模型的上下文工程新规
actions.text_en: Tonight, run `/doctor` in a Claude Code project you use regularly and see what it flags as trimmable in your CLAUDE.md and skills. Anthropic's blog today essentially published its own grading rubric: for newer-generation models, old rigid rules in the system prompt, like a hard cap on comment length, got replaced with more abstract judgment calls like match the surrounding code's style, and Claude Code's system prompt got cut by over 80% with no drop in benchmark scores. Concretely: run `/doctor` first and note what it flags as redundant or safe to hand over to the model's judgment; then pick one of your own over-specified rules and rewrite it as a description of what the result should look like rather than a step-by-step procedure, run the same task again, and see if the output holds up. If it gets worse, that rule isn't ready to go yet, but now you've actually tested it instead of guessing.
actions.source_en: Hacker News · Anthropic: new context-engineering rules for Claude 5

actions.text: 今晚花十分钟，去查一下你自己那些接了模型 API 的小工具或产品，有没有设置硬性的花费上限。今天 Hacker News 上一篇被扒出的调查显示，有一整条产业链在靠“薅”AI 厂商的免费额度和订阅套餐赚钱：运营者靠拉新用户的免费试用额度、钻订阅套餐“用量不封顶”的空子，把原本值几千美元的官方额度包装成打折套餐转卖。Simon Willison 看完这篇调查后的态度很直接：他希望自己的 LLM 应用能在花到某个金额上限时直接停止工作，而不是等账单爆炸才发现问题。具体做法：翻一下你正在跑的每一个调用模型 API 的脚本或产品，看它现在是不是“没上限、只靠信任”；如果是，去加一个每天或每月的硬性花费上限（大部分供应商控制台都有这个设置），哪怕先加一个到自己邮箱的花费预警也好，别等出问题再补。
actions.source: Hacker News · 调查：AI token转卖产业链如何运作
actions.text_en: Tonight, spend ten minutes checking whether any small tool or product you run that calls a model API has a hard spending cap. A Hacker News investigation making the rounds today traces an entire industry built on gaming AI vendors' free trials and subscription tiers: operators exploit new-signup free credits and uncapped-usage loopholes in subscription plans, repackaging what would be thousands of dollars of official credit into discounted resale bundles. Simon Willison's reaction after reading it was blunt: he wants his own LLM apps to simply stop working the moment they hit a dollar threshold he's set, rather than finding out from a huge bill. Concretely: go through every script or product you run that calls a model API and check whether it's currently running on trust alone with no cap; if so, add a hard daily or monthly spending limit (most provider consoles support this), or at minimum set up a spend alert to your own inbox before it becomes a real problem.
actions.source_en: Hacker News · Investigation: how the AI token resale industry runs

actions.text: 今晚花十分钟，把你自己维护的项目（哪怕只是 zen-digest 这样的个人项目）里对 AI 辅助贡献的态度写清楚，别留白。Debian 社区这周在投票表决四套方案，从“完全禁止 LLM 辅助的贡献”到“允许，但贡献者要为质量和安全负全部责任、并且披露自己用了 AI”，四套方案吵得很凶，说明连开源社区自己都还没有默认答案。具体做法：翻出你项目的 README 或 CONTRIBUTING，如果上面完全没提 AI 这件事，就借用 Debian 那份“允许但要披露、可担责”的思路，加两三句话，说清楚你允许别人用 AI 辅助贡献到什么程度、要不要披露、出了问题谁负责，别把这件事留给贡献者自己猜。
actions.source: Hacker News · Debian就LLM使用投票，四套方案
actions.text_en: Tonight, spend ten minutes making your own project's stance on AI-assisted contributions explicit, even if it's just a personal project like zen-digest, instead of leaving it unstated. Debian's community is voting this week on four competing proposals, ranging from banning LLM-assisted contributions outright to allowing them as long as contributors take full responsibility for quality and security and disclose their AI use, and the fact that they're split four ways shows even open source itself doesn't have a default answer yet. Concretely: pull up your project's README or CONTRIBUTING file, and if it says nothing about AI, borrow Debian's allow-but-disclose-and-be-accountable framing and add a couple of sentences spelling out how much AI assistance you allow, whether it needs disclosing, and who's accountable if it goes wrong, rather than leaving contributors to guess.
actions.source_en: Hacker News · Debian votes on LLM usage, four proposals

hands_on.title: 今晚 30 分钟：装一个 OpenWorker，让它帮你搞定一件真实的杂事
hands_on.why: 吴恩达团队开源了 OpenWorker，一个跑在你自己电脑上的 AI“同事”：桌面 App、本地优先，接了 Slack、GitHub、Jira、Notion、Google Workspace 这些常用工具。交给它的不是一个问题，而是一件具体的活，比如“整理一下我乱糟糟的日历”或者“给这个客户写一份简报”，它会自己拆解步骤、跑起来、需要动手的地方再找你确认，最后直接交付一份能用的东西，而不是一堆建议。它还有一点特别对今天的头条：调用哪家模型完全由你自己配置 API Key 决定，OpenAI、Anthropic、Google、本地 Ollama 都能换着用，不锁定一家。
steps: 去 github.com/andrewyng/openworker，下载 macOS（Apple Silicon）或 Windows 版本
首次打开时填入你自己的模型 API Key（用哪家都行：Anthropic、OpenAI、Google，或者本地 Ollama）
先接一个你真会用的工具，比如 Slack 或 Google Calendar，走一遍授权流程
给它一件具体的、有明确交付物的活，比如“把这周要回复的邮件按优先级排个列表”，而不是一个开放式问题
留意它在动手前会不会先找你确认关键步骤，这是判断这类工具能不能放心用的关键
hands_on.source: 文摘 · OpenWorker（经 TLDR AI 精选）
hands_on.title_en: Tonight, 30 minutes: install OpenWorker and hand it one real chore
hands_on.why_en: Andrew Ng's team open-sourced OpenWorker, an AI coworker that runs on your own machine: a local-first desktop app that connects to Slack, GitHub, Jira, Notion, and Google Workspace. You don't hand it a question, you hand it a task, like clean up my messy calendar or draft a client brief, and it breaks the task into steps, runs them, checks in with you before anything consequential, and delivers an actual finished artifact instead of a list of suggestions. One detail ties it straight to today's lead story: which model it calls is entirely up to you, since you supply your own API key, and OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or a local Ollama model all work interchangeably, with no vendor lock-in.
steps_en: Go to github.com/andrewyng/openworker and download the macOS (Apple Silicon) or Windows build
On first launch, plug in your own model API key (any of Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, or a local Ollama model works)
Connect one tool you'd actually use, like Slack or Google Calendar, and go through its authorization flow
Give it one concrete task with a clear deliverable, like sort this week's emails into a priority list, rather than an open-ended question
Notice whether it checks in with you before taking consequential steps. That's the real test of whether a tool like this is safe to trust

meta_read: 今天五条消息都在追问同一个问题：该给 AI 多少信任，边界画在哪。Anthropic 的答案是往前多迈一步：模型判断力够了，就把管着它的规矩往回收，系统提示词砍掉八成，赌的是模型能接住这份信任。Debian 的答案正好相反：面对同一批工具，一个成熟的开源社区选择往回缩，四套投票方案没有一套是“完全不管”，最宽松的那套也要求披露和担责，等于把“我们还不完全信任无监督的 AI 产出”正式写进社区规则。这两条放在一起说明，“该信 AI 多少”没有统一答案，每个场景自己算账：厂商离模型能力更近，敢往前赌；社区要为下游千万个发行版的可靠性负责，只能往回收。第三条 token 转卖产业链讲的是厂商自己划的信任边界被人找到了漏洞：免费试用和不封顶套餐留出的操作空间，被一整条产业链拿去套利，说明“信任”一旦没有硬性的量化上限兜底，就会被人从数字上找到破绽，光靠信任本身撑不住。斯坦福那份就业数据给整个讨论泼了一盆冷水：不管厂商还是社区吵得多凶，这套“该给 AI 多少空间”的问题反映到真实就业市场上的幅度其实很小，唯一站得住脚的冲击集中在应届生这一小群人身上，说明舆论对 AI 能力和影响的想象，走在了真实证据前面很远。最后 FLUX-mimic 提醒一句：这场关于“信任边界画在哪”的讨论，很快就不只发生在代码和聊天记录里了，视频模型的能力已经能直接喂给机器人做动作控制，而且已经进了真实工厂测试，边界要往物理世界挪的时候，出错的代价会比多写一行注释或者转卖几个 token 贵得多。
meta_read_en: Line up today's five items and they're all answering the same question: who gets to decide how much trust to extend to AI, and where the line gets drawn. Anthropic's own answer is to lean further in: now that the model's judgment is good enough, pull back the rules governing it, cut the system prompt by 80%, and bet that the model can carry that trust. Debian's answer runs the opposite direction: facing the same tools, a mature open source community is pulling back instead. None of its four competing vote proposals says do nothing, and even the loosest one demands disclosure and accountability, formally writing we don't fully trust unsupervised AI output yet into community policy. Put side by side, these two show there's no single answer to how much to trust AI; it's a calculation each context makes for itself. A vendor sitting closer to the model's own capability can afford to bet forward, while a community responsible for the reliability of thousands of downstream distributions can only pull back. The third item, the token resale industry, is what happens when a vendor's own trust boundary has a hole in it: the room left open by free trials and uncapped usage tiers got found and arbitraged by an entire supply chain, showing that trust without a hard, quantified ceiling behind it eventually gets picked apart at the numbers. Stanford's jobs data throws cold water on the whole argument: however loudly vendors and communities are fighting over how much room to give AI, the real-world jobs market has barely moved, with the one impact that actually holds up concentrated on a narrow slice of recent graduates, meaning public imagination about AI's capability and impact is running well ahead of the actual evidence. The last item, FLUX-mimic, is a reminder that this argument over where to draw the trust boundary won't stay confined to code and chat logs much longer. A video model's capability can now feed straight into robot motor control, and it's already being tested on a real factory floor, and once the boundary moves into physical space, the cost of getting it wrong is a lot higher than an extra line of comments or a few resold tokens.

learned: 读台账确认，最近十条主线都在解“怎么运行一个多 agent 循环”这一轴：评测分级、效果分层、供应商容错、证据分级、harness 可移植性审计。今天 Anthropic 官方博客给了一个不同轴的信号：管住模型的规矩本身也该跟着模型代际往回收，不是所有代际都该用同一套 prompt 写法。老一代模型需要密集规则和例子才能管住输出，新一代模型（Opus5 这一档）判断力已经足够强，继续堆规则只会浪费上下文；Anthropic 自己把 Claude Code 给新模型用的系统提示词砍掉了八成以上，跑分没掉。

回头看我自己实际在用的 skill 文件，比如这份 daily-digest 本身，写法明显偏老派：大量条文式的硬规则（比如对 banner 字数、action 数量、每个字段要不要_en 都有精确规定），例子和反例塞得很满，同一条要求在不同小节里会重复出现。Anthropic 这篇文章点名的三种可以精简的地方——规则改判断、例子改接口设计、一次性塞满改按需加载——在这份 skill 里都能找到对应的位置，但云端环境不能碰~/.claude，只能先把这个具体观察记下来，留给笔记本 Claude 去动手改。
new_capabilities: 🎯（云端提议，待笔记本采纳）“技能瘦身：把 daily-digest 这类长 skill，按 Claude5 代新规则做一次精简”：具体做法，笔记本 Claude 下次运行时先跑一次`/doctor`，看官方工具本身给出哪些建议，再手动过一遍 daily-digest 的 SKILL.md，挑出里面写成硬性条文、但其实新一代模型凭判断就能做对的规则，试着改写成描述“结果长什么样”而不是“按哪几步做”的句子，删之前跑一次同样的每日流程做对比，输出质量不掉就留着精简版，掉了就说明这条规则还得留着当硬约束。这不是重新发明前十条讲“怎么调度运行子任务”的那根轴，是完全不同的一层：不是运行时怎么调度模型，而是写给模型看的 skill/prompt 本身该怎么写，随着模型代际升级，写法也该跟着变。灵感来自今天 Anthropic 官方博客《新一代模型的上下文工程新规》。调用意图：“写或改一份 skill/系统提示词之前，先假设新一代模型能处理更抽象的判断题，只有验证它接不住才补硬规则；定期检查已有的长 skill 里有没有可以从硬规则降级为判断题的地方，跑一次真实任务对比着做，别凭感觉删。”
learned_en: Reading the ledger, the last ten lines all sit on one axis: how to run a multi-agent loop well, from binary evals through effort tiering, provider fail-over, evidence-graded defaults, and harness-portability audits. Today's Anthropic blog post signals a different axis entirely: the rules governing a model should shrink as the model generation improves, and one prompt-writing style shouldn't apply across every generation. Older models needed dense rules and examples to keep output in check; newer models (the Opus 5 tier) now have strong enough judgment that piling on more rules just wastes context. Anthropic cut Claude Code's own system prompt for newer models by over 80%, with no drop in benchmark scores.

Looking back at a skill file I actually use, this very daily-digest skill, its writing style is clearly old-school: dense with rigid, rule-like specifications (exact character counts for the banner, exact counts for actions, precise rules for which fields need an _en sibling), packed with examples and counter-examples, with the same requirement repeated across different sections. All three trimmable patterns Anthropic's post names (rules become judgment, examples become interface design, upfront loading becomes progressive disclosure) have a matching spot in this skill, but the cloud environment can't touch ~/.claude, so this observation is just recorded here for laptop Claude to act on.
new_capabilities_en: 🎯 (cloud-proposed, pending laptop adoption) "Skill diet: trim a long skill like daily-digest per the new Claude-5-generation rules": concretely, next time laptop Claude runs, first run `/doctor` to see what the official tool itself flags, then manually pass over daily-digest's SKILL.md and pick out rules written as rigid specifications that a newer-generation model could actually get right through judgment alone, try rewriting them as a description of what the result should look like rather than a step-by-step procedure, and run one real daily cycle to compare before deleting anything; keep the trimmed version if output quality holds, and keep the rule as a hard constraint if it doesn't. This isn't reinventing the prior ten ledger lines about how to schedule and run subtasks; it's an entirely different layer, not how a model gets dispatched at runtime, but how the skill/prompt written for the model should itself be written, and that should shift as model generations improve. Inspired by today's Anthropic blog post, "The new rules of context engineering for Claude 5 generation models." Invoke intent: "before writing or editing a skill or system prompt, assume a newer-generation model can handle a more abstract judgment call, and only add a hard rule once you've verified it can't; periodically check existing long skills for rules that can be downgraded to a judgment call, testing against a real task rather than deleting by feel."

items.title: Anthropic公布Claude 5代模型的新提示词规则：从立规矩到信判断
items.title_en: Anthropic publishes new context-engineering rules for Claude 5 models: from rules to judgment
items.author: Anthropic官方博客 · Hacker News
items.flag: ⚠️ HN 评论区里有开发者反馈，Opus5 这两天实际用下来，删掉老规则之后有时反而更啰嗦、更容易犯粗心的错误；这套“少写规则”的建议是 Anthropic 自己的方法论，不是所有场景都验证过，删规则前最好自己跑一遍对比。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ Several HN commenters report that in the two days since Opus 5 shipped, cutting old rules sometimes made it more verbose or more prone to careless mistakes. This less-is-more guidance is Anthropic's own methodology, not something validated for every use case, so it's worth testing your own before/after before deleting rules.
items.summary: Anthropic 将自己为 Claude Code 编写系统提示词的方法论整理成博客公开，核心是一次立场转变：老一代模型需要靠密集的规则和例子约束输出，新一代模型（Opus5 这一档）判断力已足够强，继续堆规则反而浪费上下文、限制能力。文章给出了几组“以前怎么写、现在怎么写”的对照：规则变判断，以前写“注释不能超过一行”这种死规定，现在改成“照抄周围代码的注释密度、命名习惯、风格”这种描述结果而非步骤的判断题；例子变接口设计，以前靠堆工具调用示例去约束模型如何使用工具，现在把心思花在把工具参数和枚举选项本身设计清楚，让模型不用看例子也知道该怎么做；一次性塞满上下文变按需加载，像代码评审规范这类细节，改成放进“技能（skills）”里，模型真正用到时才去查，而不是一开始就塞进系统提示词；重复的指令直接删掉，工具使用说明只在工具描述里写一遍，不再在系统提示词里重复。文章给出的最实的数据：靠这套新方法论，Claude Code 给新一代模型用的系统提示词被砍掉八成以上，跑分没有下降。文章还建议 CLAUDE.md 这类项目说明文件要“写得轻”，只留真正反直觉、容易踩坑的细节，别写成一本手册；官方同时推出了 `claude doctor`（Claude Code 里可以直接跑 `/doctor`）这个诊断工具，帮你自动检查系统提示词、CLAUDE.md、skills 里哪些内容该精简。HN 评论区吵得也凶：有人喜欢这个方向，也有人觉得这是把可迁移的 .md 配置往 Anthropic 自家专属工具链上迁，会增加锁定；还有开发者反馈说 Opus5 上线这两天，实际用下来变化没那么理想，删了以前管用的规则之后，模型有时反而更啰嗦或者更容易犯粗心的错误。
items.summary_en: Anthropic turned its own methodology for writing Claude Code's system prompt into a public blog post, and the core message is a reversal: older-generation models needed dense rules and examples to keep their output in check, but newer models (the Opus 5 tier) now have strong enough judgment that piling on more rules just wastes context and boxes the model in. The post walks through several before/after pairs. Rules become judgment: instead of a rigid rule like no comment longer than one line, the new guidance says match the surrounding code's comment density, naming, and style, describing the desired result rather than a step-by-step procedure. Examples become interface design: instead of stacking tool-call examples to constrain usage, the effort goes into designing clear tool parameters and enumerated options so the model knows how to use a tool without needing examples. Loading everything upfront becomes progressive disclosure: details like code review conventions move into skills that the model only pulls in when actually needed, instead of being crammed into the system prompt from the start. Repeated instructions get cut outright: tool usage guidance lives only in the tool's own description, not copied again into the system prompt. The most concrete number in the post: this approach let Anthropic cut Claude Code's system prompt for newer models by over 80%, with no drop in benchmark scores. The post also recommends keeping files like CLAUDE.md lightweight, holding only genuinely counterintuitive gotchas rather than turning it into a manual, and it introduces a new diagnostic tool, claude doctor (run as /doctor in Claude Code), that automatically flags what in your system prompt, CLAUDE.md, and skills can be trimmed. Reaction on HN split: some like the direction, others see it as pulling portable .md configuration toward Anthropic's own proprietary tooling and increasing lock-in, and several developers reported that in the two days since Opus 5 shipped, results have been mixed, with some finding that after cutting rules that used to work, the model got more verbose or careless in places.
items.why: 本期头条，也是对做 agent/skill 这行最直接能用的一条：它把“给模型写多少规矩”这件事从经验之谈变成了官方方法论，还给了具体的删减比例做参照。可迁移的判断：以后写系统提示词或 skill，先假设模型能处理更抽象的判断题，只有验证过它接不住才补规则，而不是反过来一上来先把能想到的规矩都堆上去。带着 flag 看：HN 评论区里也有开发者反映，实际把老规则删掉之后，Opus5 有时反而更啰嗦、更容易出小错，说明这套新规则不是无脑照搬，删之前最好自己验证一遍。
items.why_en: The issue's lead, and the most directly usable item for anyone building agents or skills. It turns how many rules to give a model from folklore into an official methodology, with a concrete trim ratio to benchmark against. The transferable judgment: when writing a system prompt or skill going forward, assume the model can handle a more abstract judgment call first, and only add an explicit rule once you've verified it can't handle the abstract version, rather than front-loading every rule you can think of. Read with the flag: several HN developers report that after cutting old rules, Opus 5 sometimes got more verbose or careless instead of better, so this isn't a rule to apply blindly; test the before/after yourself before deleting anything.

items.title: 调查扒出AI token转卖产业链，靠薅免费额度和订阅漏洞赚钱
items.title_en: Investigation exposes an AI token resale industry built on gaming free trials and subscription loopholes
items.author: vectoral.com · Hacker News
items.flag: ⚠️ 文章里“每花 1 美元能买到相当于多少美元官方额度”这类折扣倍数，评论区指出换算方式有争议、说法本身也不清楚，作者自己也承认表述模糊；别把具体倍数当成精确数字，只看“折扣确实很大、来源确实可疑”这个方向性结论。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ The specific discount multiples in the article, like how many dollars of official credit one dollar buys, are disputed in the comments and even the author admits the phrasing is unclear. Treat the exact multiples as fuzzy, and take away only the directional conclusion: the discounts are real and the sourcing is shady.
items.summary: 一篇调查文章扒出一整条围绕 AI 模型 token 转卖的灰色产业链，主要活跃在中国。核心手法是滥用开源代理软件（文章点名 one-api 和它的分支 new-api，这两个项目本身是正经的负载均衡工具），把多个官方 API 密钥或订阅账号池在一起，再对外拆分转卖便宜 token。便宜的来源主要有三种：薅新用户免费试用额度、钻订阅套餐“用量不封顶”的空子把成本摊薄、以及用被盗支付方式开的账号。买家里，有人图便宜，有人想绕开地区限制，也有人专门收集这些 token 拿去做模型蒸馏。评论区吵得很凶：有人算了下文章给的折扣数字（比如“425 元人民币买到价值 3333 美元的官方额度”），发现换算本身就有争议，作者也承认这句话表述不清；也有人辩论这到底算不算“欺诈”，一派认为这就是变相的信用卡欺诈，另一派说这更像是钻订阅合同空子的灰色套利，很难一刀切定性。Simon Willison 在自己博客里转发并评论了这篇文章，说这提醒了他，AI 厂商得在“给 API 密钥设置严格的花费上限”这件事上做得更好，他自己的原话是希望自己的 LLM 应用能在花到设定的额度上限时直接停止工作，而不是等账单爆炸才发现问题。
items.summary_en: An investigative piece exposes an entire gray-market industry built around reselling AI model tokens, mostly active in China. The core technique abuses open-source proxy software (the article names one-api and its fork new-api, both legitimate load-balancing tools), pooling multiple official API keys or subscription accounts together and reselling cheap tokens on top. The cheap supply comes from three main sources: farming new-user free trial credits, exploiting uncapped-usage loopholes in subscription tiers to dilute cost, and accounts opened with stolen payment methods. Buyers include people chasing cheap prices, people working around regional restrictions, and some collecting tokens specifically for model distillation. The comments argued hard: some ran the numbers on the article's headline discount figure (a package advertised as $3,333 of official Anthropic credit for 425 RMB) and found the math itself disputed, with the author admitting the phrasing was unclear; others debated whether this even counts as fraud, with one camp calling it disguised credit-card fraud and another calling it gray-area arbitrage on subscription-contract loopholes that's hard to cleanly classify. Simon Willison reposted and commented on the article on his own blog, saying it's a reminder that AI vendors need to get better at offering strict spending caps on API keys; in his own words, he wants his LLM apps to simply stop working the moment they hit a dollar threshold he's set, rather than finding out from a huge bill.
items.why: 本期的模型经济学对照条，跟头条形成互补：头条讲的是模型厂商怎么对待模型本身（信不信任模型的判断），这条讲的是模型厂商怎么对待自己的计费边界（有没有把“用量上限”这道门关严）。可迁移的判断对任何接了模型 API 的产品都适用：免费试用和“不封顶”套餐是留给用户的体验空间，同时也是留给灰产的套利空间，如果自己的产品或工具没有硬性花费上限，这个口子迟早会被人找到。今晚能做的事，是去检查一下自己接的模型 API 有没有设花费上限（详见二版）。
items.why_en: The issue's counterpart to the lead, on the economics side: the lead is about how a model vendor treats the model itself (how much to trust its judgment), while this one is about how a vendor treats its own billing boundary (whether the usage-cap door is actually shut). The transferable judgment applies to any product that calls a model API: free trials and uncapped tiers are user-experience room, but they're also arbitrage room for gray-market operators, and if your own product or tool has no hard spending cap, that gap will eventually get found. Tonight's move: check whether the model APIs you rely on have a spending cap set (see Action 2).

items.title: Debian就是否允许LLM辅助贡献投票，四套方案吵起来
items.title_en: Debian votes on whether to allow LLM-assisted contributions, four competing proposals
items.author: Debian项目 · Hacker News
items.flag: ⚠️ 投票文本里“使用”和“辅助”这两个词到底怎么界定，评论区吵得很凶，连开发者自己都没统一答案；任何团队想照抄这套规则前，得先想清楚自己怎么定义“用了 AI”。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ HN commenters argue hard over how the vote text's use and assistance are even defined, and Debian developers themselves don't have a unified answer; any team borrowing this framework needs to first decide how it defines used AI.
items.summary: Debian 项目在自己的投票系统上提交了一份正式提案，要在几套方案中选一个作为社区对“LLM 辅助贡献”的正式立场。方案 A 最严：直接在社区宪章里写明禁止一切 LLM 辅助的贡献，涵盖打包、官方软件、文档和网站，理由有四条：版权归属不清、输出质量不可靠（“一个 LLM 生成的包会混杂编造的版权信息，基本没法用”）、新人靠 LLM 糊弄贡献学不到真本事还拖累审核者，以及训练数据本身获取方式不道德。方案 B 相对宽松：允许 AI 辅助，但要满足六个条件，包括确认 AI 工具的条款不影响自由软件的分发方式、贡献者对质量和安全负全部责任、有实质性 AI 辅助要向审核者披露、大批量或自动化的贡献要提前沟通、避免把项目敏感数据传给外部工具。方案 C 介于中间：呼吁贡献者尽量别用 LLM，但承认完全禁止不现实，要求所有直接对外的沟通（邮件、bug 报告、帖子）必须由人亲自写，使用 LLM 要披露，各子项目自己的禁令要被尊重，违反视为行为准则问题处理。方案 D 聚焦“接受但担责”：允许 AI 辅助做 Debian 相关工作，但提交者要自己核实质量、真正理解自己提交的内容，并在 commit 里标注用了 AI。HN 评论区分歧很大：有人觉得这标志着 Debian 要完了，也有人反驳说 Ubuntu 这类大量下游发行版都建在 Debian 之上，这套规则等于给整个生态定调；技术讨论集中在“使用”和“辅助”到底怎么界定，比如用 Claude Code 定位 bug、给修复建议，但最终由人手动改代码测试，这算不算“辅助”，连开发者自己都没有统一答案。
items.summary_en: The Debian project opened a formal vote choosing among several proposals for the community's official stance on LLM-assisted contributions. Proposal A is strictest: it would write a ban on all LLM-assisted contributions, covering packaging, official software, documentation, and websites, directly into the Social Contract, citing four reasons: unclear copyright status, unreliable output quality (an LLM-produced package will have a mixture of contents, including imaginary copyright, and will generally be unfit), new contributors leaning on LLMs without learning real skills while straining reviewers, and the training data itself being obtained unethically. Proposal B is more permissive, allowing AI assistance under six conditions: verifying the AI tool's terms don't conflict with free-software distribution, contributors taking full accountability for quality and security, disclosing significant AI assistance to reviewers, discussing bulk or automated contributions beforehand, and avoiding tools that transmit sensitive project data externally. Proposal C sits in the middle: it asks contributors to avoid LLMs while acknowledging a full ban is impractical, requiring humans to draft all direct communication (emails, bug reports, posts), disclosure of LLM use, respect for individual sub-projects' own bans, and treating violations as Code of Conduct issues. Proposal D focuses on accept-but-be-accountable: it allows AI assistance for Debian-specific work but requires submitters to verify quality themselves, genuinely understand what they're submitting, and mark AI usage in commits. Reaction on HN split hard: some see this as a sign Debian is dying, others counter that since a huge number of downstream distributions like Ubuntu are built on Debian, this policy effectively sets the tone for the whole ecosystem; the technical argument centers on how use and assistance even get defined, for example whether using Claude Code to locate a bug and suggest a fix, with a human then manually editing and testing the code, counts as assistance, and even Debian's own developers don't agree.
items.why: 本期唯一的开源治理条，跟前两条形成对照：前面两条讲的是厂商怎么对待模型、对待自己的计费边界，这条讲的是使用方（一个成熟开源社区）第一次正式给“能不能用 AI 贡献”划边界。可迁移的判断对维护任何项目的人都适用：与其让 AI 辅助贡献这件事留白让每个贡献者自己猜，不如学 Debian 这几套方案的思路，至少写清楚“允许到什么程度、要不要披露、出问题谁负责”这三件事。今晚能做的事，是去看看自己维护的项目有没有对这件事表过态（详见三版）。
items.why_en: The issue's only open-source governance item, contrasting with the first two: those cover how a vendor treats the model and its own billing boundary, while this one is about a user of these tools, a mature open source community, formally drawing a line on whether AI-assisted contributions are allowed for the first time. The transferable judgment applies to anyone maintaining a project: rather than leaving AI-assisted contributions unaddressed for every contributor to guess about, borrow Debian's framing and at minimum spell out how much is allowed, whether it needs disclosure, and who's accountable if it goes wrong. Tonight's move: check whether your own project has ever stated a position on this (see Action 3).

items.title: 斯坦福研究：AI对就业的冲击，被吹得比数据显示的更猛
items.title_en: Stanford brief: AI's real jobs impact is smaller and narrower than the hype claims
items.author: Stanford SIEPR · Hacker News
items.flag: ⚠️ 报告自己也承认，2022 年那波“AI 暴露度越高的岗位招聘越少”的数据，时间点上更可能跟当时美联储加息、疫情后招聘过量的回调撞在一起，AI 的具体因果要到 2024 年之后才更站得住脚，别把相关性直接当成因果性。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ The brief itself acknowledges that the 2022 pattern of hiring declines in AI-exposed occupations coincides with the Fed's rate hikes and a post-pandemic hiring correction, and that AI's causal role only becomes more plausible after 2024. Don't read the correlation as confirmed causation.
items.summary: 斯坦福经济政策研究所整理了一批关于 AI 对就业市场真实影响的实证研究，想跟当下“AI 就业末日”的舆论做个对照。Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 此前预测 AI 可能消灭一半白领岗位、把失业率推到 20%，正是报告想核实的说法之一。报告给出几条主要结论：整体就业层面，AI 目前造成的冲击很小，暴露度最高的那批岗位（比如软件开发）过去几年失业率涨幅（0.77 个百分点）甚至比暴露度最低的岗位（0.85 个百分点）还要小，招聘岗位数量也在正常增长；采用了企业级 AI 的公司两年后员工数平均反而涨了 10%。但对应届毕业生来说情况明显更难：2026 年初新毕业生失业率涨到 5.6%，比三年前高 1.6 个百分点。Brynjolfsson 等人的研究把年轻员工比作“矿井里的金丝雀”，在客服代表和软件开发这两个 AI 高暴露度岗位里，年轻员工的雇佣数量从 ChatGPT 发布后开始下滑，同岗位年长员工的雇佣却基本稳定甚至在涨。不过报告也提醒，这个时间点跟美联储 2022 年加息、疫情后过量招聘的回调撞在一起，很难把“下滑”完全归因于 AI，2024 年之后 AI 的因果关系才更站得住脚。生产力方面的证据好坏参半但总体偏正面：一项呼叫中心的实验里，AI 助手让新手客服的问题处理量涨了 30%，但对资深客服几乎没有提升，甚至答复质量略微下滑；GitHub Copilot 让写代码任务快了 56%，提升主要集中在经验少的程序员身上。企业采用 AI 的速度在加快，但行业之间很不均匀。报告的落脚点是：现在下“AI 引发就业末日”或者“AI 对就业毫无影响”这两个结论都为时过早，真正值得盯住的是应届生和资深员工之间正在拉开的差距。
items.summary_en: Stanford's Institute for Economic Policy Research (SIEPR) compiled a body of empirical research on AI's real impact on the labor market, meant to check it against the current AI jobs apocalypse discourse, one target being Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's prediction that AI could wipe out half of white-collar jobs and push unemployment to 20 percent. The brief's main findings: at the aggregate level, AI's current impact on employment is likely small, with unemployment among the most AI-exposed occupations (like software development) rising less over the past few years (0.77 percentage points) than among the least-exposed occupations (0.85 points), job postings still growing normally, and firms that adopted enterprise AI seeing employment grow 10 percent on average two years later. For recent graduates, though, conditions are notably tougher: new-grad unemployment hit 5.6 percent in early 2026, up 1.6 points from three years earlier, and Brynjolfsson and coauthors describe young workers as canaries in the coal mine, since employment among young workers in two AI-exposed occupations, customer service representatives and software developers, has declined since ChatGPT's launch, while employment among older workers in the same occupations stayed roughly stable or kept growing. The brief cautions, though, that this timing coincides with the Fed's 2022 rate hikes and a post-pandemic hiring correction, making it hard to attribute the decline entirely to AI; AI's causal role only gets more plausible after 2024. Productivity evidence is mixed but generally positive: in one call-center experiment, an AI assistant raised novice agents' issue-resolution rate by 30 percent with almost no gain for experienced agents, whose response quality even dipped slightly; GitHub Copilot sped up coding tasks by 56 percent, with gains concentrated among less-experienced programmers; enterprise AI adoption is accelerating but very unevenly across industries. The brief's bottom line: it's too early to conclude either an AI jobs apocalypse or that AI has no effect on jobs at all; what's actually worth watching is the widening gap between recent graduates and experienced workers.
items.why: 本期唯一一条给前几条模型经济学泼冷水的数据条，跟前三条形成对照：前面几条都在讲 AI 能力和使用边界怎么变，这条提醒你，这些变化目前反映到真实就业市场上的幅度，比舆论和 AI 领袖自己说的要小得多，唯一站得住脚的例外是应届生招聘在明显收缩。可迁移的判断：招聘和团队规划时，与其被“AI 要取代所有初级岗位”这种笼统说法带着走，不如去看具体数据，把注意力放在真正在收缩的那个细分群体（应届、低经验岗位）上，而不是笼统恐慌或者笼统乐观。
items.why_en: The issue's one item that pours cold water on all the preceding model-economics stories: the earlier items are about how AI's capabilities and usage boundaries are shifting, and this one reminds you how small that shift currently looks in the real jobs market compared to what pundits and AI leaders themselves claim, with the one exception that actually holds up being a real contraction in entry-level hiring. The transferable judgment: when hiring or planning a team, rather than getting swept up in AI will replace all junior roles as a blanket claim, look at the actual data and focus attention on the specific group that's genuinely contracting (new grads, low-experience roles) instead of blanket panic or blanket optimism.

items.title: FLUX 3把视频生成和机器人控制放进同一个模型，已经在奥迪工厂试跑
items.title_en: FLUX 3 unifies video generation and robot control, already piloting on Audi's factory floor
items.author: Black Forest Labs（经Latent Space/TLDR AI精选）
items.author_en: Black Forest Labs (curated via Latent Space/TLDR AI)
items.flag: ⚠️ FLUX-mimic 在奥迪工厂的部署，目前报道里只写了“测试中”，具体规模、良品率、是否已经正式投产都没有披露，先当一个方向性信号看，别当成已经量产的结论。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ Coverage of the FLUX-mimic deployment at Audi only says testing, with no disclosed scale, yield, or confirmation of production use. Treat it as a directional signal, not a finished production story.
items.summary: Black Forest Labs 发布 FLUX 3，这是一个将图像、视频、音频和动作预测纳入同一架构联合训练的多模态模型，而非将多个专用模型拼凑而成。新增能力包括文字生成视频、图片生成视频、视频生成视频（可处理参照画面）、视频自带音轨、多语言对话、关键帧到视频的可控转场，风格覆盖从纪实到电影感的大跨度，还支持“agentic 链式生成”，能将多个镜头串成连贯的多镜头序列。最值得关注的落地案例是 FLUX-mimic：它将 FLUX 3 的底座模型与 Mimic Robotics 的灵巧操作经验结合，用机器人和可穿戴设备采集的数据训练，仅需一块本地 GPU 即可运行。团队认为这证明了“看懂视频”本身可直接转化为“控制机器人”的能力，视频世界模型与机器人动作控制正在变成同一套底层能力的两种表现。目前 FLUX-mimic 已在奥迪实际工厂环境中测试。商业化方面，FLUX 3 Video 已开放早期访问，官方还预告了一个开放权重的 Dev 版本。
items.summary_en: Black Forest Labs released FLUX 3, a unified multimodal model jointly trained across image, video, audio, and action prediction, rather than a collection of separate specialized generators. New capabilities include text-to-video, image-to-video, and video-to-video generation with reference-image handling, native audio accompanying video output, multilingual dialogue, controllable keyframe-to-video transitions, style range spanning documentary-feel footage to cinematic looks, and agentic chaining that strings multiple shots into a coherent multi-shot sequence. The most notable applied case is FLUX-mimic: combining FLUX 3's backbone with Mimic Robotics' dexterous-manipulation expertise, trained on data collected from robots and wearables, and able to run on a single on-prem GPU. The team argues this proves that understanding video translates directly into robot control, meaning video world models and robot motor control are becoming two expressions of the same underlying capability. FLUX-mimic is already being tested in a real Audi factory environment. On the commercial side, FLUX 3 Video is open for early access, and the company has previewed an open-weight Dev version to come.
items.why: 本期唯一一条将镜头拉至“模型能力如何长出真实世界生产力”的条目，与前三条形成互补：前几条讲模型在数字世界（代码、聊天、贡献）的边界如何划定，这条提醒你边界正向物理世界延伸——视频生成模型的能力已能直接喂给机器人控制，且非实验室演示，而是真正进了汽车厂的产线测试。可迁移的判断：如果你的工作涉及机器人、硬件或任何“看视频学动作”类应用，这条比单纯的模型跑分更值得盯，因为它说明“哪个模型看视频看得准”以后可能直接决定“哪个机器人动作做得对”。
items.why_en: The issue's only item that pulls the camera to how model capability turns into real-world productivity, complementing the first three: those cover how boundaries are being drawn in the digital world (code, chat, contributions), while this one is a reminder that the boundary is now extending into the physical world. A video-generation model's capability can already feed straight into robot control, and it's not a lab demo, it's genuinely in a car factory's production-line testing. The transferable judgment: if your work touches robotics, hardware, or any watch-video-learn-motion application, this is worth tracking more closely than a plain benchmark score, since which model reads video most accurately may soon directly decide which robot's movements come out right.
